description: Niobium is a light grey, crystalline transition metal with symbol Nb and atomic number 41. It is a lustrous, ductile, paramagnetic metal that is slightly less electropositive and more compact than zirconium, with chemical properties very similar to tantalum.
uses: Niobium is used mostly in alloys, particularly in special steels such as those used in gas pipelines, where it enhances strength by scavenging carbide and nitride. It is used in superconducting materials for MRI scanner magnets, jet and rocket engines, welding, nuclear industries, electronics, optics, and jewelry. The metal is also used in nuclear industries where neutron-transparent structures are desired due to its low neutron capture cross-section.
characteristics: Pure niobium has a Mohs hardness rating similar to pure titanium and ductility similar to iron. It oxidizes very slowly in Earth's atmosphere and is corrosion-resistant. Niobium becomes a superconductor at cryogenic temperatures with the highest critical temperature of elemental superconductors at 9.2 K, and it has the greatest magnetic penetration depth of any element. When very pure, it is comparatively soft and ductile, but impurities make it harder.
